From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Vance <dpo@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TIA scope & UK Addendum — alignment on routing safeguards

Hi Sarah / Acme legal team,

Following up on our onboarding kickoff — we want to align on the transfer impact assessment (TIA) scope and the UK Addendum (IDTA) expectations so we can produce the evidence package you need. High-level asks:

- Can you confirm the primary EU/UK-to-US routing patterns you expect us to cover in the TIA (e.g., storage regions, cross-border backups, logging pipelines)?
- Any subprocessor-specific controls or attestations beyond the standard SOC2 + contracts?
- Timeline for receiving your redlines to the proposed UK Addendum — can we target next Thu (May 27)?

Attached are: 1) a TIA scoping template (spreadsheet) with suggested sections; 2) our initial draft UK Addendum for your legal review. If helpful, we can run through the template in a quick 30-min call and capture the details live.

Proposed next steps (from our side):
- We’ll prepare a subprocessor map export and a short controls matrix matching our safeguards to TIA sections.
- If you require additional technical evidence (packet traces, egress lists), let us know the format and retention window.

Thanks — happy to loop in Rishi for the subprocessor map and Lauren for legal ops.

Best,
Monica Patel
Head of Privacy & Compliance (Americas)
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_tia_scoping_template.xlsx, proposed_uk_addendum_draft.docx
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@acme-corp.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, legal@acme-corp.com
Cc: Marcus Vance <dpo@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: TIA scope & UK Addendum — alignment on routing safeguards

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the packet and the draft — this is helpful. A few quick answers and requests:

- Routing: please include both primary (EU region: eu-west-1) and DR/backup paths (US-east-1). We also need clarity on any third-country routing (APAC) that touches EU data.
- Subprocessors: we require an explicit attestation for any subprocessor that persists personal data outside the EU/UK — include country, purpose, and retention.
- Evidence: our procurement team typically asks for (a) certs (SOC2 type II, ISO 27001), (b) recent penetration test summary, (c) a short architecture diagram showing data flow, and (d) a subprocessor index CSV.

On the UK Addendum: legal has a couple of carve-outs around law enforcement access and emergency disclosure wording. I’ve attached our baseline evidence checklist for your reference. We’ll aim to have legal redlines to your doc by May 26, but that depends on a quick clarifying call about the routing notes above.

Can we do a 30-min sync tomorrow (May 21) at 9am BST / 1am PT? If that time doesn’t work for you, propose alternatives.

Best,
Sarah Lewis
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Acme Corp
Attachments: acme_required_evidence_list.pdf

Hi all — quick update from the subprocessor side. Attaching the current export and a short notes file. Key points:

- Subprocessor map attached as CSV (subprocessor_map_2027-05-20.csv) — includes processing country, data categories, contract start date, and certificate links.
- No APAC regions persist EU/UK customer personal data (we use APAC regions for ephemeral compute only; data at rest for EU/UK customers is in eu-west-1 and us-east-1).
- For any subprocessor that may incidentally replicate logs for debugging, we can surface retention windows and implement IP-based ACLs to prevent broad access.

Timeline: I can assemble the controls matrix matching our TIA template sections by EOD Monday (May 24). If Acme needs anything sooner, tell me which specific evidence items to prioritize and I’ll accelerate.
